items.title: Trump says Iran sent 'big present' as US prepares troop surge
items.description: The US president suggests a mystery gift "worth a tremendous amount" is aiding diplomatic efforts to end the war and comes as he reportedly prepares to send a major airborne force to the region.

items.title: Breaking: Inflation falls slightly in February to 3.7 per cent
items.description: However, the latest monthly data does not capture the recent rise in energy prices caused by the war in the Middle East, which began on February 28.

items.title: Jetstar reduces flights between New Zealand and Australia due to rising jet fuel prices
items.description: Jetstar announces it is reducing flights between Australia and New Zealand due to the rising cost of jet fuel as a result of the war in the Middle East.

items.title: Live: Tehran tells UN 'non-hostile' ships can go through strait if they coordinate with Iran
items.description: Iran has told the UN Security Council and the International Maritime Organization that "non-hostile vessels" may transit the Strait of Hormuz if they coordinate with Iranian authorities. Follow live.

items.title: Ships are escaping the Strait of Hormuz and one is headed for Australia
items.description: The Japanese-owned Iron Maiden will be the first known ship to dock in Australia after it was stranded in the Persian Gulf when the US and Israel first bombed Iran on February 28.

items.title: 'Something really shifted': Inside the software company that laid off 40pc of its staff
items.description: As big tech companies sack staff and say AI will pick up the slack, workers are left to grapple with what's really going on.

items.title: Man dies in police custody in Darwin after being put in back of police vehicle
items.description: Authorities have confirmed a man died in police custody in Darwin's northern suburbs overnight, after he was "arrested without incident".

items.title: ABC managing director apologises to audience, amid strike action
items.description: A majority of staff who voted rejected the broadcaster's latest pay offer on the three-year enterprise bargaining agreement, which paved the way for the strike action.

items.title: Could Cyclone Narelle come as far south as Perth?
items.description: Tropical Cyclone Narelle is now barrelling towards Western Australia. Could this unusual cyclone make it all the way to Perth, and how does climate change affect it?

items.title: Katherine braces for possibility of second major flood this month
items.description: Residents in Katherine are bracing for the possibility of major riverine flooding today, which would mark the second significant weather event to rock the town in a month.

items.title: In Australia's most food insecure suburbs, lines for aid are doubling
items.description: Most areas across Australia are dealing with food insecurity as food relief services say demand is growing. It comes as experts warn the price of groceries are likely to increase due to the war in the Middle East.

items.title: They lived in spare rooms and motels, their teen years 'stripped away'
items.description: Spare bedrooms, couches, and cars hide the stories of Australia's youth homeless crisis. But they are stories that also reveal a grit and ambition to defy the statistics.

items.title: Married at First Sight expert Mel Schilling dies, aged 54
items.description: Schilling's husband, Gareth Brisbane, took to social media on Tuesday night to reveal the news.

items.title: Governments announce $2b bailout for Boyne aluminium smelter
items.description: Rio Tinto, the federal and state governments have struck a landmark partnership to secure the long-term future of the Boyne aluminium smelter.

items.title: Waste collectors warn bin services may stop if diesel not found soon
items.description: Waste collectors say they are struggling to acquire diesel and many are operating at "unsustainable" losses, putting the collection of household bins and commercial waste under threat.

items.title: How Melbourne ended up with the biggest comedy festival in the world
items.description: The very first Melbourne International Comedy Festival launched 40 years ago, and while it's kept its scrappy charm, things look pretty different today.

items.title: Couples on sleeping separately and if it's helped — or hindered — their relationships
items.description: Snoring, shift work, parenting and health — you shared the many reasons why you no longer sleep in the same bed as your partner, and whether it's been a positive move for sleep and the relationship.

items.title: Travel quiz: Do you have the stamina to complete this trip?
items.description: Which country has the dong as its currency? And where would you dine on tteokbokki?

items.title: Location of Brisbane's new 63,000-seat stadium unveiled
items.description: New artist impressions showing the interior of the 63,000-seat arena have also been released.

items.title: Two more arrested over grandfather's alleged kidnapping murder
items.description: Two more people have been arrested in relation to the alleged mistaken identity kidnapping and murder of Sydney grandfather Chris Baghsarian.

items.title: Former England captains question findings of Ashes review
items.description: Former England captains and current player Jonny Bairstow question the findings of an internal review into a disastrous Ashes campaign, which saw the team's leaders maintain their positions.

items.title: 'So lucky': Burke warns failed Perth bomb attack could have killed many
items.description: The home affairs minister says Australia was "so lucky" to avoid mass casualties during the attempted Australia Day bomb attack in Perth and admits the nation was slow to recognise the gravity of the alleged terrorist act.

items.title: Basil Zempilas not ruling out preference deal with One Nation at WA election
items.description: Basil Zempilas is "not fearful" of the soaring rise of Pauline Hanson's One Nation in the west, but acknowledges his WA Liberals will need to decide whether to direct preference votes to the controversial party or distance themselves.

items.title: E-bike power crackdown and age limits introduced in NSW
items.description: The NSW government has recently announced staged reforms to improve safety for e-bike riders and pedestrians. This is what it'll mean for the community.

items.title: Want to sleep deeper? Vivid dreams might help
items.description: People woken during vivid and immersive dreaming feel like they've had a deep sleep — even when their brain is in a lighter sleep state, according to a new study.
